chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad informed us, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), that he said:
Surely, the example of Abu Talib is like that of the Companions of the Cave, who kept their faith secret and displayed polytheism, so God gave them their reward twice.

key_terms.أَبُو طَالِبٍ: Abu Talib — the Prophet's uncle and guardian, whose faith is a major theological debate between Sunni and Shia Islam
key_terms.أَجْرَهُمْ مَرَّتَيْنِ: Their reward twice — a double divine recompense for both concealment and true belief
key_terms.أَسَرُّوا الْإِيمَانَ: They kept faith secret — concealed their belief internally
key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْكَهْفِ: Companions of the Cave — the 'People of the Cave' mentioned in Surah al-Kahf (18:9-26), who fled persecution
key_terms.أَظْهَرُوا الشِّرْكَ: They displayed polytheism — outwardly appeared as pagans
key_terms.مَثَلُ: Example, parable, similitude — used to draw an instructive comparison

ai.seo_question: Was Abu Talib a secret believer? What does Imam al-Sadiq say about Abu Talib's faith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) draws a parallel between Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle and protector, and the Companions of the Cave (Ahl al-Kahf) from Surah al-Kahf. Both concealed their true faith outwardly while practicing polytheism in appearance, yet their sincere inner belief earned them a double reward from God. This hadith addresses the longstanding theological controversy about Abu Talib's faith, affirming — from a Shia perspective — that Abu Talib was a secret believer who concealed his Islam to protect the Prophet, just as the Companions of the Cave concealed their faith under a pagan king.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq al-Talaqani (rh) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Al-Mundhir b. Muhammad informed us from Ja`far b. Sulayman from `Abdullah b. al-Fadl al-Hashimi from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said:
Surely, the example of Abi Talib is like that of the companions of the cave, who kept the faith a secret and feigned paganism, so Allah gave them their reward twice.
